validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE / CLASSIFICATION / DUPLICATE all clear, and confirmed at a HIGHER bar than the harvested wiki pool offered. None of the 13 citations harvested off gem.wiki/Rover_Pipeline (the page shared by all four Rover rows: P0392, P2438, P2604, P2635) name this specific sub-project -- they cover Phase 1A's 2017 FERC approval, the final-two-laterals 2018 announcement, 2017 construction-era protests/leaks (Livingston Daily, MLive, DeSmog, PBS, Grist), the EIA pipeline-projects workbook (generic aggregate), Rextag (paywalled map product), and the 2021 $40M FERC penalty (Reuters) -- so I went to open-web search per the SOP's escalation path. Found and read to exhaustion: FERC approved Rover Pipeline LLC's request (Docket CP20-36, order dated April 16, 2020) to raise Rover's mainline capacity by 175 MMcf/d (3.25 -> 3.425 Bcf/d), achieved -- per both independent accounts -- 'by the use of efficient operating conditions without any additional construction or modifications to existing facilities' (enerknol.com) / 'without any new equipment and without any additional cost' (marcellusdrilling.com, dated Jan 2020, describing the pending request). This is a genuine, separate FERC docket action distinct from Phase 1 (P0392, CP15-93, 711 mi/1700 MMcf/d, in service 2017), Phase 2 (P2438, len 0, 1550 MMcf/d, the 2018 final-laterals build), and the Wick Meter Station Expansion (P2635, len 0, 300 MMcf/d, West Virginia-scoped) -- no duplicate/merge action against any of the other three Rover rows. Correctly classified: interstate FERC-jurisdictional gas transmission capacity expansion, Gas commodity. Confirms the current LengthKnown=0/blank Diameter are CORRECT, not a data gap -- this is exactly the 'expansion with no new physical pipe' pattern the SOP calls out, achieved through compression/operating efficiency on the existing mainline, so I did not 'fix' either cell. Two mutually independent sources (Marcellus Drilling News, an independent Marcellus/Utica trade blog that read the FERC filing directly; EnerKnol, a separate policy-research publisher summarizing the FERC order text) corroborate the 175 MMcf/d figure, the no-new-equipment mechanism, and the April 16, 2020 approval date. A THIRD, current (April 2026) independent source -- marcellusdrilling.com's report of a temporary capacity cut for compressor-station maintenance -- additionally confirms Rover, and by extension this capacity addition, remains in active operating service as of five months before this sweep.

I could not find independent evidence either confirming or refuting a delay specific to CP20-36, so this is flagged as a caveat for verification rather than an asserted error -- absence of a mention in two short trade-press notes is suggestive, not proof, that no delay occurred.
